gaps.text: In-line measurement of Process temperature with bioreactor temperature probe

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: synchronised Raman and NIR spectra merged into one augmented matrix with block scaling, as in the published process example. Both probes must sample the same well-mixed spot and the data must be normalised to a common time step. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs or it is dropped.)
Achievable accuracy, detection limits or response times for glucose and lactate in a cell culture medium with any of the shortlisted methods.
Sterilisable or autoclavable probe designs for bioreactor insertion.

items.finding: The text notes that temperature sensitivity of certain bands creates drawbacks for aqueous solutions in specific spectral ranges.
items.how_it_applies: This highlights that temperature monitoring and control should be evaluated when assessing spectroscopic setups for aqueous cell culture media.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This source observation addresses general aqueous solutions rather than the specific bioreactor temperature probe setup or cell culture conditions.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
